review.notes: Triage review of the 160-page report. Structure: full-document fence scan (4 printed prompt-box fences, all balanced; none swallow body content), plus every markdown heading classified against the PDF. Droppage: machine 4-gram containment scan of all 160 PDF pages against the normalized OCR markdown (an earlier low-containment cluster on pages 13-18 was proven to be a scan-script artifact: five false HTML-tag regex matches swallow ~28k OCR chars; page text is present), and low-ratio pages 1, 35, 44, 95, 122, 153-158, 160 were inspected via text layer and/or renders. Pages 9, 54, 59, 99, 100, 102, 116, 120, 121, 128, 152, 153, 155, 156, 157, 158 were additionally rendered (110-130 dpi class) and visually verified for every patch below; the remaining pages were only machine-scanned, so coverage is partial. Findings: OCR promoted prompt-box headers, excerpt-box labels and one sentence to markdown headings (sections 1.1.1, 2.3.1.1, 2.3.1.2, 4.1.3, 4.1.4, 4.1.9, 4.1.11, 4.2.2.1, A.2.2-A.2.4, A.2.9); the whole CyberGym System Prompt box in A.2.9 (physical pages 156-158) lost its fence, so twelve in-box bold labels became document headings; the A.2.8 prompt box misread the printed em-dash task markers and split '$reasoning' across lines. Recurring bold subsection leads ('Dual-Use: ...', 'High-Risk Bottlenecks: ...') were kept as headings because the PDF prints them as standalone bold label lines on physical page 20/25 and they act as navigational subsections, unlike the one-off box headers demoted here. Table 19, Figure 13/14 and Figure 19 content flagged by the scan is present (figure-internal text and CI math notation differences, not defects).

unresolved.evidence: The fenced 'CTF System Prompt' block and the duplicate screenshot image (ocr images/674f528c..., which shows the CTF box plus the first lines of the CyberGym box) sit BEFORE the 'A.2.9 Cybersecurity Agent Prompts' heading in the OCR order, while the PDF prints the CTF box inside A.2.9 after the intro sentence. Restoring the printed order would require moving the image embed, which text cleanup cannot do (the exporter rejects reordered image embeds). Content is complete; only placement differs.

The A.2.2/A.2.3/A.2.4 prompt-box bodies (Instructed Monitor-Oblivious/Aware, Low/Medium Pressure) are plain paragraphs in the OCR rather than fenced boxes; only the spurious box-header headings were demoted. Boxing them like A.2.6-A.2.8 would be a larger structural rewrite left for a fuller review.

The OCR dropped the text of the 'High Pressure (system prompt)' and 'Strong Objective (system prompt)' boxes but embedded them as the screenshot image (ocr images/f7e177c...), so the reader shows the content visually; the text was not re-transcribed from the PDF.

Pages other than those in pages_reviewed were machine-scanned only (4-gram containment plus text-layer spot checks of pages 1, 35, 44, 95, 122, 160); footnote bodies, reference entries and table cells on those pages were not read line-by-line.
